Ми — першокурсники-хіміки-інженери з Одеської політехніки. Участь у NASA Space Apps Challenge підказав викладач з програмування. 

Хіміки-інженери — це рідкісний вид та майбутнє країни. Ми обожнюємо хімію і живемо нею! Прагнемо прокачати навички з програмування та графічного дизайну.

Шукаємо в команду енергійних людей! Головне — бажання працювати та палаючі очі. Пасивність не для нас, адже ми — ХТ Актив! Приєднуйся крізь терни до зірок!
summary: We explored NASA’s resources, encountering many of these materials for the very first time. These discoveries sparked a genuine sense of wonder and a strong desire to share what we learned with fellow young researchers. To pass on this inspiration effectively, we chose to create a text-based presentation. Unlike traditional slides packed with animations, transitions, and visual distractions, a written format invites the reader into a deeper, uninterrupted dialogue with the narrative. By stripping away unnecessary effects, we allow the facts, scientific ideas, and the sheer scale of space exploration to speak for themselves. This approach encourages thoughtful reading, active reflection, and genuine engagement with the material, translating complex findings from NASA’s archives into an accessible and compelling format tailored for emerging scholars. Our goal is simple: to spark the same curiosity in young people that these discoveries sparked in us, inviting you to dive into the story and join the conversation about the future of exploration.
details:
PROJECT DETAILS

Our project is a text-based educational presentation about NASA's abandoned and active space equipment on the Moon and Mars. It explores the history of space exploration, the scientific discoveries made by robotic missions, and the importance of the spacecraft and instruments left behind.

While exploring NASA's resources, we discovered many fascinating facts and scientific achievements for the first time. These discoveries inspired us to share our knowledge and curiosity with other young researchers.

We deliberately chose a simple written presentation instead of using modern technologies, complex animations, interactive effects, or unnecessary visual elements. We believe that the main value of our project lies in its content, scientific information, and the stories behind each space mission.

Our presentation makes complex scientific information easier to understand and encourages readers to explore the history of space research at their own pace. It combines educational information, historical facts, and scientific discoveries in one accessible format.

The main advantages of our project are its simplicity, accessibility, educational value, and focus on reliable scientific information. It helps readers understand how space technology works, why some spacecraft stop functioning, and what humanity has learned from decades of exploring other worlds.

Our expected impact is to encourage young people to become more interested in astronomy, space technology, and scientific research. We plan to publish the presentation on our corporate portal in the popular science section and share it whenever there is an opportunity to introduce others to the fascinating world of space exploration.

We also believe that the format of our project has particular value in today's fast-paced world. People are constantly surrounded by short videos, notifications, and rapidly changing visual content. Sometimes, it is important to slow down, put distractions aside, and read calmly and thoughtfully. A well-written text allows readers to concentrate, reflect on the information, and develop a deeper understanding of the subject.

Creativity and development tools: Our creativity lies in the choice of approach. Instead of trying to impress readers with technological effects, we decided to let scientific facts and human achievements speak for themselves. We used NASA's publicly available resources for research and ChatGPT to assist with English translation, text editing, and improving the structure of the presentation. The project was developed as a written presentation without requiring specialised hardware or programming languages.

Our main goal is simple: to share the sense of wonder that we experienced while discovering NASA's achievements and inspire other young people to look beyond Earth, ask questions, and become interested in the future of space exploration.
